sectors.name: Technology
themes: Indonesia's domestic tech hardware names (MSKY, MSI) are decoupling from US semis, driven by local data-center capex and government digital-infrastructure spending that will sustain through 2025.
Global optical and networking components (ALAB, GLW, LITE) benefit from AI-cluster interconnect buildouts, a durable multi-year cycle independent of handset or PC demand.
US-listed chip names (ARM, ON) remain hostage to macro rates and export-control headlines, making them tactical trades, not core holdings, for Indonesia-based portfolios.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in MSKY and MSI on momentum persistence, but cap exposure to US semis (ARM, ON) given NORMAL signal and mixed ID/US tape. Rotate into ALAB and GLW for optical/network demand resilience. Trim LITE on profit-taking risk. Maintain 5-7% tech weight, favor ID-listed names over US ADRs for currency and local liquidity alpha.

sectors.name: Financials
themes: Indonesian financials are decoupling from US rate sentiment, with domestic liquidity and loan growth now the primary price driver, favoring banks with strong retail exposure.
Insurance-linked financials (ABDA, ASMI) are gaining structural traction as penetration rises and digital distribution lowers acquisition costs, creating durable fee-income growth.
Mid-cap banks (BDMN, NICK) are benefiting from NIM stabilization as deposit competition eases, but differentiation hinges on asset-quality discipline in consumer and SME books.
sectors.ai: Buy BDMN and ABDA on strength: both are re-rating on improved asset quality and NIM stability, with BDMN's auto-loan recovery and ABDA's insurance-led fee income driving outsized gains. Trim NICK and PADI into rallies—their moves are liquidity-driven, not fundamental. Hold MET for dividend yield, but avoid chasing WIDI/SBIN until volume confirms.

themes: Indonesia's geothermal pipeline is accelerating on government-mandated PLN offtake contracts, making PGEO and BREN structural winners regardless of global clean-energy sentiment.
Biomass co-firing mandates at existing coal plants are creating a durable domestic demand floor for TPIA and MPOW, insulating them from US policy swings.

US climate-tech names like CWEN remain hostage to Fed rate expectations, while IDX renewable listings benefit from a weaker rupiah and local institutional flows — a persistent divergence favoring Jaka
sectors.ai: Buy the dip in Indonesian geothermal and biomass names — PGEO, BREN, and TPIA are absorbing global rate pressure with domestic demand and 2025 capacity catalysts intact. sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small-cap FMCG names are benefiting from a post-Ramadan restocking cycle and rural demand recovery, driving outsized gains vs. large-cap staples.
Domestic consumption remains insulated from global slowdowns, with IDX consumer stocks outperforming US counterparts by 32bps, supported by stable inflation and government subsidies.
Momentum is concentrated in micro-caps with low float, creating sharp re-rating opportunities but also elevated reversal risk, favoring traders over long-term holders.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap FMCG momentum names (PDES, IATA, AGAR) on domestic consumption resilience and low base effects, but avoid chasing overextended moves without volume confirmation. Favor staples with pricing power and distribution reach as IDX consumer outperforms US peers; trim into strength if RSI exceeds 75.

sectors.name: Infrastructure
themes: Indonesia's new capital project (IKN) is entering its peak construction phase, funneling sustained contracts to domestic contractors like SOLA and IPOL through 2025.
Gas infrastructure names (RGAS) benefit from the government's downstreaming mandate and rising industrial gas demand, a multi-year structural tailwind independent of global commodity cycles.
Cement (SMGR) is leveraging the housing deficit program and toll-road expansion, with pricing power improving as oversupply normalizes and logistics costs ease.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in SOLA, IPOL, and RGAS as their outsized gains reflect genuine order-flow catalysts in toll roads and gas distribution, not beta. SMGR's steady advance signals cement demand is firming ahead of the election-year infrastructure push. Trim US-exposed names like VRT on rate-cut delays; rotate into domestic contractors with visible government backlog.

M&A and innovation cycles in cardiovascular and lab equipment are driving premium multiples, rewarding early movers with pipeline catalysts.

sectors.name: Entertainment, Media & Consumer Services
themes: Indonesia's digital advertising spend is compounding at 15%+ annually, structurally favoring pure-play media names like MDIA and FUTR over legacy broadcasters.
The shift to programmatic DOOH and connected TV is creating a two-tier market: high-margin tech-enabled platforms outperform asset-heavy operators, pressuring DOOH and FOX valuations.
Consumer services resilience hinges on middle-class discretionary income growth, but rising food and energy costs are squeezing MAPB's retail margins, making selective exposure critical.
sectors.ai: Buy the pullback in TMPO and FAST on volume-confirmed breakouts; rotate out of DOOH and FOX into MDIA/FUTR for higher beta. Watch VIVA as a laggard catch-up play if IDX media breadth holds above 1.2x. Trim MAPB into strength, as consumer services face margin compression from input costs.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesia's crypto adoption is driven by remittance and inflation hedging, favoring stable, asset-backed tokens over speculative altcoins.
Regulatory clarity from Bappebti and OJK is shifting institutional flows toward compliant, audited assets like PAXG and XAUT, reducing exposure to unregulated meme coins.
Global privacy-coin demand (XMR, BDX) is structurally rising as surveillance frameworks tighten, creating a persistent premium for anonymity-focused digital assets.
sectors.ai: Rotate into privacy and gold-backed tokens (XMR, PAXG, XAUT) as regulatory noise caps broad altcoin upside; 币安人生's +7.9% spike is sentiment-driven and not repeatable. Trim LIT/PI into strength, hold BDX for cross-border flows. For Indonesia, overweight XAUT as a rupiah-hedge given BI's easing bias and gold's local premium.
